# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — ⚠ EMPTY HANDOVER, framework-synthesized from the commit reason (the optimizer wrote no entry of its own — see the `optimizer_context_warning` event):
INDECISIVE: only 0% of val tasks produced a valid score (< 60% required). The evaluation measured the infrastructure, not the edit — not counted as a rejection.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** UNRESOLVED (not judged; champion unchanged) · val=0.000 Δ=-0.415 · fixed={—} · broke={0, 13, 26, 28, 31, 36, 41, 43, 46, 47} · unresolved={10, 11, 25, 3, 37, 40, 48, 8} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them). — the measurement could not separate this edit from re-measurement noise, so it is NOT evidence against the edit. Its batch was still reverted. To resolve it, re-measure it under a FRESH tag (re-running the same tag REPLACES its rollouts) or with more trials in ONE evaluation; do not redesign it on this round's numbers, and do not re-derive it as a new idea.

## Iteration cand_0002 — normalize malformed write-args (payment_id/dob/insurance) that pydantic rejects
- Changes I made:
  - book_reservation.py (cluster: write-arg SHAPE): added in-body `_norm_payments` (map `id`/`payment_method_id`→`payment_id` when missing; whole-float amount→int), `_norm_passengers` (map `date_of_birth`&variants→`dob` when missing), `_norm_insurance` (non-enum→`yes`/`no`). Plus additive docstring stating the EXACT required keys for the weak reader.
  - book_reservation.py (cluster: recoverable error): on the primitive's "does not add up" error STRING, append an explicit ACTION-NEEDED instruction to re-call with amounts summing to the total. Only runs on a failed booking.
  - update_reservation_passengers.py (same dob-key normalization + docstring).
- Expected effect + why safe: server-side `Payment`/`Passenger`/`Insurance` pydantic models REJECT the malformed shapes the model emits (verified against the real models), so the write raises and DB never matches → MISS. Normalizing to the canonical shape lets the write land. Targets failing tasks {8,14,15,20,22,23,25,29,35}. SAFE/BOUNDED: none of the 10 passing tasks {0,13,26,28,31,36,41,43,46,47} call book_reservation or update_reservation_passengers, and correct shapes pass through unchanged — so no passing trajectory can change. Malformed shapes appear ONLY in failing tasks (180 id-key, 60 dob-key, 64 insurance="none", 230 extra-type occurrences across non-infra trials).
- Building on prior RESULTS: cand_0001 scored 0% valid (a LOAD/infra failure, not a content signal — its batch was reverted, nothing to build on content-wise). I kept strict one-top-level-function-per-file + AST-verified load to avoid repeating that. Did NOT re-try anything from it (it left no diff).
- Refuted hypotheses: none proven yet (only 1 prior iter, and it was infra-void).
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: (a) action-STALL — agent narrates a change then never writes, often because it presents a WRONG price and the simulated user declines, or the reservation is basic_economy (cannot be modified → must cancel+rebook). Needs a price-compute or cancel+rebook composite tool, designed against gold; not attempted this round to avoid regression. (b) baggage free-allowance miscount (nonfree_baggages) — needs the membership×cabin allowance rule. (c) send_certificate stalls — policy-governed, must NOT be loosened.
- Plateau signal: n/a (first real content iteration). If normalization lands, next lever = a composite cancel+rebook / price-compute tool for the stall cluster.
- Focus next iteration: build a price-computation helper (per-cabin seat prices + insurance 30/pax + 50/nonfree-bag) so the agent presents correct totals and the user proceeds; and a cabin-change composite that routes basic_economy changes through cancel+rebook.
